title: cut.yml runs-on: give the cut runner its own label (camcraft-cut) and keep skull/egg off the Linux post-merge pool until their UI tests start

body:
Found during the cut of v0.25.0 (release PR #3266).

`cut.yml` runs its jobs on `[self-hosted, linux]`. Each Linux post-merge runner matches that label set, so the release gate can land on any of them. Three facts from the cut:

1. Run 44964821090 landed on wopr-2. A post-merge run ran at the same time on wopr, which looks like the same host. The step "Release gate tier" was cancelled after one minute, with no test run.
2. The UI test binaries abort in 0-2 s with `exit -1` on some runners (#3258). Those failures occurred on skull, egg and wopr.
3. From about 00:13Z on 2026-11-22, no Linux runner was online. Run 44965350029 stayed queued, and the release gate ran locally (the fallback of the `release-cut` skill).

What the runners API shows (2026-11-22). It shows no owner of a runner, so this issue names only the labels:

| Runner | Labels |
|---|---|
| cheese, dude, skull, egg, len-pm, wopr-2 | `self-hosted`, `Linux`, `X64`, `camcraft-post-merge` |
| uma | `self-hosted`, `Linux`, `X64`, `uma-linux`, `camcraft-post-merge` |
| wopr | `self-hosted`, `camcraft-post-merge` |
| m3 | `self-hosted`, `macOS`, `ARM64`, `m3-macos`, `camcraft-pr-test` |

Proposed change (a process and workflow change; it needs the maintainer's approval as a `.github` change):

- Add the label `camcraft-cut` to one or more healthy Linux runners. Change `runs-on` of both jobs in `cut.yml` to `[self-hosted, linux, camcraft-cut]`.
- Keep skull and egg out of the Linux post-merge pool until their UI test binaries start (#3258).
- Change the `runners` skill to match.

This is not on the cut list of v0.25.0. It does not block a cut.
